newsitem.title: DUBAI: Yemen denies contacts with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Yemen denies contacts with Israel.

text.p: Yemen on Monday dismissed Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy's talk of secret contacts between the states as "mere fabrication".
"There is no truth to reports that our two countries are discussing opening interest offices," a Yemeni government spokesman in the capital Sanaa told Reuters by telephone.
"Reports about talks between officials from the two countries are mere fabrication," the spokesman at the presidential palace said.
Israel's foreign minister said earlier in the day the two countries were discussing establishing official ties through opening interest offices.

"Discussions and normalisation of ties with Israel would only follow a just and comprehensive peace in the region and an Israeli withdrawal from occupied Arab land in Palestine, the Golan Heights and south Lebanon," the Yemeni spokesman said.

Levy, speaking to Israel Radio during a visit to China, confirmed a report in the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper that Eitan Benzur, director-general of the Israeli Foreign Ministry, secretly met Yemen's foreign minister in Europe at the weekend.

"Even before this we sent a special emissary who brought a message from me," Levy said. "We are maintaining channels of communications and now we are heading...towards the main thing -- another country with which we can open an interest office."
Levy said he could give no further details until Israel and Yemen issued a joint announcement.
Yedioth Ahronoth said Yemen had agreed as a first stage to allow up to 10,000 Israelis of Yemeni extraction to visit and Israeli companies to invest in the country.
Israel already has a foothold in the Arabian peninsula, with trade missions in Oman and Qatar. Oman has a trade office in Tel Aviv.
Oman and Qatar said last year they had put contacts with Israel on ice to protest against hardline Israeli policies toward Palestinians.
